notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: By headlines of 21 November, two days after the Shenzhen declaration, drones disabled the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, two tankers were hit leaving Hormuz off Oman, Iran's Revolutionary Guard shot down a US drone as Iran talks were said to stall, and one of more than 110 Russian missiles fired at Ukraine was reported to hit Poland. The Nasdaq erased its gains for the year, gold fell more than $2,000 an ounce from its peak and bitcoin dropped below $55,000, while Trump attacked the Federal Reserve for keeping rates high. Since 18 November attackers had reached the FBI's crime records database, the US Agriculture Department, the European Commission's servers and Transport for London's photocard records. India's home minister Amit Shah backed the Siang dam against protesters, Taipei's mayoral race argued over solar panels on the Feicui reservoir and Bogotá warned of water and power rationing. From the day before, Estonia had set 1 December to close its Russian crossings and German pupils struck against conscription.
moved: The thread on Europe's security after the declaration reached the sea on 21 November: Sparta II disabled by drones in the Gulf of Finland, two tankers hit leaving Hormuz and a US drone shot down by Iran, with talks reported as about uranium, NATO and Russia's prewar demands. The Gulf war's events returned through this thread, not the Iran thread.

Two Iran thread expectations of 2 November failed on 21 November: no report of Brent below $105 on resumed talks, and none of a 5% one-day rise after a Gulf incident, though tankers were hit that day. The Pope's Peru expectation and a 4 November expectation of a European party leader claiming the US result also failed.

A new thread read the fall of 20 and 21 November as the cost of money: the Nasdaq erased its year's gains, gold fell more than $2,000 from its peak and bitcoin dropped below $55,000. It sits beside the data centre and AI financing threads, which read the same fall through chips and listings.

Two threads began from subjects the site's notebook had kept for days: breaches of records people must give the state, with public bodies about half of four days' list, and new hydro and solar power placed on water already promised to farms and towns.
silent: The shared systems thread has had no narrative since 18 November. The 21 November breaches of the FBI, the Commission and Transport for London came in a new thread as data taken, not systems stopped, so this looks like the editions' division more than the world moving on.

The thread on interceptor stocks has had no narrative since 18 November. More than 110 Russian missiles struck Ukraine on 21 November, in the thread on Europe's security, with no report on stocks or production.
The trade deals thread has had no narrative since 18 November. No trade agreement came in the 19 to 21 November narratives; after APEC week that may be the world moving on as much as the sample.
The Iran war thread stays silent since 11 November by the editions' division: its tankers and drone on 21 November came in the thread on Europe's security.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, talks and reach
threads.text: On 26 October the join was the Gulf running talks and strike preparations. From 27 October to 5 November it followed the Hormuz price shock to jet fuel, mortgages, wages and rates. The war was reported paused on 8 November; on 10 November oil fell on talk of talks; on 11 November producers invested as if Hormuz would stay unsafe. Since then its events have come in other threads: a US strike on Qeshm on 17 November, Iranian strikes on US assets on 18 November, and on 21 November two tankers hit leaving Hormuz and a US drone shot down, in the thread on Europe's security. On 21 November two of its 2 November expectations failed: no report of Brent below $105 on resumed talks, and none of a 5% one-day rise after a Gulf incident, though tankers were hit that day.
threads.direction: After a pause on 8 November and a turn to talks, the US and Iran were reported striking each other from 13 November, and by 21 November the attacks were on tankers and a drone over the strait while talks were said to stall.

threads.label: Governments setting pump prices mid-war
threads.text: Begun on 7 November: Italy would not extend its diesel excise cut, Portugal adjusted its fuel tax discount and Taiwan's CPC held pump prices after absorbing NT$34.07 billion, joined as governments handing the war's fuel price back to drivers. After four editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 12 November with an unlinked narrative marked firm: Pakistan cut petrol and diesel prices, Chile resubmitted a bill freezing fuel prices until February, Greece set €32 million for islanders' sea transport and Indonesian ferry operators asked to raise fares, with crude below $90. Its case against says the decisions move in different directions and none names Hormuz. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to early December.
threads.direction: It has moved from governments ending fuel tax cuts to governments keeping pump prices in their own hands and paying the gap from budgets as crude fell below $90.

threads.label: War energy shock turned into equipment orders
threads.text: Begun on 6 November and not linked by its edition to the Iran thread, though it starts from the same war. Iran says two tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Siemens Energy says a Middle East power push is straining gas turbine supply, a Chinese solar cell line runs at full capacity, Adani Green turns to batteries for India's grid, and an agency finds the energy crisis speeding renewables in emerging economies. The join is that buyers who cannot lower the price of imported fuel are buying equipment to need less of it. Its case against says Siemens Energy's backlog and China's solar capacity predate the war. No narrative has carried it since 6 November, so it is silent. Gas sought beside electrification began a separate thread on 10 November.

threads.label: Housing: state drives, outside money and work
threads.text: On 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing with Portugal investigating police at housing protests. On 6 November the Chronicle revived it, by judgment, when foreign buyers made 16% of Portuguese purchases as prices hit records. On 11 November it was revived again, by judgment, with a narrative marked tentative: millions of Spaniards struck over housing three weeks before a general election, a rush of withdrawals hit China's payroll housing fund, and employer-linked homes were offered in Tianhe and Taiwan. Its case against says Spain has a shortage and China a slump. On 17 November Spain's strike and Porto's housing camp came in a new thread on Europe's weekly protests, which joins them with wages and prices; the Chronicle has not revived this thread for it.
threads.direction: It has moved from states building homes, to prices set by buyers from outside, to housing argued over through strikes, payroll funds and employers.

threads.label: Shared systems failing, from outages to patches
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand, it ran through AI-led US growth, borrowing and the Nvidia case to 12 November. From 12 November it followed shared systems stopping: a Microsoft outage at British councils and Australia's federal police, the FAA's nationwide halt, the fallback left to households on 14 November, and on 17 November faults hard to tell from attacks. On 18 November South Korea's Digital Daily blamed a flood of patches for AI-found flaws for failures at the NSA, in finance and in aviation. No narrative has carried it since, so it is silent; data centres returned on 20 November as public money, and breaches of public records began their own thread on 21 November. Its case against says the patch cause rests on one outlet.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and borrowing to public services stopping when one system fails, to who holds the backup, to telling a fault from an attack, and by 18 November to patches for AI-found flaws named as a cause.

threads.label: AI labs financed by suppliers, then public shareholders
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 10 November: TSMC was reported investing NT$32 billion in OpenAI and Anthropic as Anthropic's draft prospectus showed a listing of up to $64.4 billion. Its expectation that Anthropic would cut or delay its listing failed on 17 November. The Chronicle revived it on 18 November for an unlinked narrative: Anthropic priced at $83 a share as the ECB compared the AI build to subprime. On 19 November Anthropic passed $3 trillion on its first day while Taiwan's index fell below 40,000 with 45 settlement defaults. The fall that followed came in other threads: on 20 November the Nasdaq fell 5.37% and CoreWeave dropped below its listing price, and on 21 November the Nasdaq erased its year's gains as gold and bitcoin fell too. Its case against says large first-day rises are normal for new listings.
threads.direction: It has moved from chip suppliers funding the AI labs, to the labs selling shares to the public at record prices, to who took the first-day gain while other technology shares fell.

threads.label: Courts and heads of state given the last word
threads.text: Begun on 1 November and marked tentative: Poland's president and Tusk's government fighting over the Constitutional Tribunal, Egypt's debate on amending the constitution and Madeira's revision; its case against said only Poland's was a crisis. After six editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 7 November, by judgment: lawyers say Vučić's pardons could go to Serbian courts and Strasbourg, Malaysia's Attorney General seeks an audience with the King over Najib Razak's pardon, Taiwan's cabinet refuses to countersign an Elderly Welfare Act, and a Nigerian court voids Atiku's candidature. No narrative has carried it since 7 November. On 19 November its 1 November expectation was kept when Financial News reported South Korea's ruling party would push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Jo Hee-de, a move against one member of the court rather than its powers.
threads.direction: It moved from fights over who controls courts and constitutions to who has the last word on pardons and laws already passed.

threads.label: Chinese makers' gains and others' answers
threads.text: Begun on 3 November: SCG's chief executive called China's cheap exports a fact of life, Thailand raised taxes on imported electric cars, and Tata Motors and Iveco formed a group. It was revived on 7 November, by judgment, when Musk said Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck and BYD's Yangwang opened pre-orders for a 2.08 million yuan car. On 8 November its own edition carried it on, with Tesla suspending orders for the Cybertruck's entry version, NIO claiming a car a minute and Yangwang launching in Abu Dhabi. On 10 November, with no narrative, The Independent reported Musk axing the Cybertruck with refunds, keeping the 7 November expectation of another US carmaker cutting an electric pickup, though by Tesla itself. No narrative has carried it since 8 November, and no headline here reports a sale lost to a Chinese maker.
threads.direction: It moved from producers elsewhere merging or taxing to meet Chinese goods, to producers elsewhere retreating, and by 8 November to Chinese makers selling abroad at both the cheap and the luxury end.

threads.label: Soldiers sent against disorder, gangs and smugglers
threads.text: Begun on 5 November, marked tentative: Indonesia's troops in Jakarta, the army's account of a riot in Aceh, Pakistan's army for Punjab by-elections, a Bangladeshi soldier killed raiding traffickers at Teknaf, Lebanese army raids and a French bill widening when police may fire. After eleven editions without a narrative it was resumed on 19 November, marked plausible, as crime fought as war: Haiti's forces fought gangs for a corridor with Salvadoran troops in the country, Colombia's president counted a tenth bombing and weighed asking Congress for US troops, fishermen sued Washington over a drone strike at sea and the OAS called a session on organised crime. On 20 November La Dépêche reported France's parliament definitively adopting the law presuming police use of weapons lawful, keeping the 5 November expectation; the headline came in the youth protest thread. Its case against says the military role in each is decades old.
threads.direction: It has moved from soldiers keeping order on home streets to armies, aircraft and foreign troops fighting gangs and smugglers, with results counted as deaths and strikes.

threads.label: Regulators targeting platforms' recommendation systems
threads.text: Begun on 6 November. The European Commission accused TikTok of breaching EU rules through its content recommendation system, and Google, Meta and TikTok are suing to block a California law restricting addictive social media features for children. China's broadcasting regulator opened a two-month campaign against vulgar and homogenised AI micro-dramas after removing 75,000 titles, and Democrats are preparing AI bills for Congress. The join is that the thing regulated is the system choosing what a user sees next, not a single post. Its case against says the three regulators want different things and only the EU and California cases are clearly about ranking design. No narrative has carried it since 6 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Failed banks and money cases reaching office
threads.text: Begun on 6 November. Paraguay's Congress resumed impeachment of President Santiago Peña over the Ueno bank crisis, Daniel Vorcaro's phone recorded 316 interactions with Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the Banco Master case, and UMNO's move to pay Najib Razak's RM50 million fine split Malaysia's coalition. On 8 November an unlinked narrative, placed here by the Chronicle, reported a court freezing the assets of Peña, described as former president, and his arrest over an estimated $809 million Ueno loss, with the Philippine vice-president answering wealth charges and opponents in Armenia and Egypt facing courts. No narrative has carried it since 8 November. On 12 November Sara Duterte's impeachment trial appeared in the new thread on leaders' children.
threads.direction: It moved from failed banks reaching people in office to courts reaching office-holders through money in general, with Peña going from impeachment proceedings to arrest in two days.

threads.label: El Niño's first weeks arriving as rain
threads.text: Begun on 7 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Keiko Fujimori is reported visiting parts of Peru's Tumbes hit by rain, and Pulzo reports that El Niño has not stopped thunderstorms and hail in Bogotá. La Patria reports a landslide bringing trees down onto an avenue in Manizales, and Brazil's Civil Defence has a 72-hour alert out. The join is that an El Niño expected as drought is arriving first as rain. Its case against says October and November are wet seasons in Colombia and south-eastern Brazil in any year, only one headline names El Niño, and only the Tumbes rain is out of season. No narrative has carried it since 7 November, so it is silent; on 21 November Bogotá's 18 November warning of water and power rationing under El Niño came in the new thread on water for power.

threads.label: Routes to work abroad rationed and deadly
threads.text: Begun on 8 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Off Lompoul in northern Senegal a pirogue capsized and at least 21 people died. In Bangladesh a lottery shortlisted 300 applicants for 112 fee-free jobs in Malaysia. A testimony in Portugal's SAPO describes shared rooms and low pay ending a migrant's stay, and in West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari promised to deport every 'Bangladeshi infiltrator'. The join is that a person's attempt to work abroad is rationed by a draw, the sea, wages or expulsion. Its case against says the lottery may be meant to cut out recruitment agents, the shipwreck's destination is not given, and four of seven headlines come from bdnews24. No narrative has carried it since 8 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Gas supply sought beside climate summit targets
threads.text: Begun on 10 November and marked tentative by its own edition. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed the last four years as the hottest on record, and COP31 set out an electrification push as the 1.5C goal slips. Deutsche Welle examined Germany's untapped gas, Japan's and Vietnam's leaders discussed an early start to an LNG project, Argentina awaited $38 billion of investment decisions for Vaca Muerta, and Brazil extended its household cooking gas programme to 2031. The join is governments securing gas while planning to electrify. Its case against says Vaca Muerta and the LNG talks are long-running. No narrative has carried it since 10 November, so it is silent; COP31 in Antalya appeared on 11 November only in the seats thread, over Israel's exclusion.

threads.label: Ukraine talks and who pays in Europe
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 10 November and marked firm by its edition. US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi produced a planned prisoner exchange of 1,000 or 1,500 a side and a US offer of 'NATO-style' security guarantees with $400 million in weapons, while Merz threatened to block the next EU budget unless every member supports Ukraine and Fico called that blackmail. Its case against says Merz's demand may belong to the 2028 to 2034 budget talks. On 11 and 12 November the talks came in the seats thread, on 13 and 17 November in the strikes thread, and on 14, 19 and 21 November in the thread on Europe's security. No narrative has carried the question of who pays since 10 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Pope Leo in politics, restraint on reform
threads.text: Begun on 11 November. Pope Leo XIV left Argentina after a Mass for three million, with Die Welt reporting that Javier Milei is on his own after the Pope's criticism, and arrived in Peru, where the government declared non-working days and Keiko Fujimori invited guests to meet him. In the same days the Vatican halted the reform process in the German diocese of Speyer. The join is one office speaking against a government's policy in South America while limiting lay-led reform in Germany. Its case against says popes have criticised Argentine economic policy for a decade and host governments always declare holidays for papal visits. No narrative has carried it since 11 November, so it is silent; on 21 November its Peru expectation failed, with no report of Leo XIV or the Vatican criticising a named Peruvian policy or official.

threads.label: Seats, borders and talks used as pressure
threads.text: Begun on 11 November and marked tentative: the CSTO stripped Armenia of its vote, Turkey excluded Israel from COP31 in Antalya, and Washington and Moscow asked Europe to choose one negotiator for the Ukraine talks. On 12 November it was carried on as entry of every kind: Israel will bar Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Washington's envoys said Europeans would join the next round, and Putin spoke of US visas for Russian Olympians. On 13 November the single-negotiator expectation failed when the EU agreed a team of five countries and EU institutions, which weakens the reading of entry as a bargaining move. Its ground passed on 14 November to the thread on Europe's security bargained elsewhere. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It moved from seats in alliances and summits to entry of every kind, and on 13 November Europe was admitted to the Ukraine talks on its own terms, against the thread's reading.

threads.label: Leaders' children judged on their own conduct
threads.text: Begun on 12 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice-president over a certificate scandal, Sara Duterte's impeachment trial is to resume after the ASEAN summit, Donald Trump Jr left an adviser's role at Kalshi over a conflict with a rival investment, and Nigeria's president congratulated his son Seyi on a traditional title. The join is what a leader's name entitles a child to hold. Its case against says the cases share a family tie and little else. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, but on 18 November its expectation was kept when R7 reported Brazil's prosecutor-general filing a criminal complaint against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for slandering Lula in a post about Maduro. A slander complaint fits the expectation more loosely than a resignation would.

threads.label: Nvidia scandal as a chip export enforcement dispute
threads.text: Begun on 13 November with a narrative marked firm that continues nothing, though the Nvidia case ran in the AI spending thread from 10 to 12 November: Bessent blamed Lutnick for Megaspeed not being blacklisted, and the Senate summoned Huang and Lutnick. Resumed on 17 November: Nvidia reported revenue up 103% and a $150bn buyback, its board refused Huang's return, and Huang will testify to the House on 1 December. Washington proposed extending chip controls to Southeast Asia, keeping a 10 November expectation. No narrative has carried it since 17 November, so it is silent; on 20 November US chip restrictions were named among causes of the sell-off and on 21 November the Nasdaq was reported erasing its gains amid Nvidia troubles, both in other threads. Its case against says diversion through Singapore and Malaysia was known before.
threads.direction: It has moved from a dispute between two US departments over who let chips reach China to new duties on the states and firms the chips pass through, while Nvidia's sales grew.

threads.label: Long-range strikes during Russia and Iran talks
threads.text: Begun on 13 November, marked plausible: as the EU named its team for the Ukraine talks, a Ukrainian drone hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, bombs went off in Moscow and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain. Resumed on 17 November, marked tentative, with crossings as targets: the Crimean Bridge twice, Kyiv's bridges with 700,000 households left without power, a rail line to Hungary and Iran's Qeshm Island. On 19 November Lenta reported Trump saying Putin is angry at Zelensky over the Crimean Bridge attack, keeping the 17 November expectation. No narrative has carried it since 17 November, so it is silent; on 20 November Russian projectiles in Poland and on 21 November attacks on ships in the Gulf of Finland and off Hormuz came in the thread on Europe's security.
threads.direction: It has moved from strikes on bases, ships and oil sites far from the fronts to strikes on bridges and islands in the days before the three-power meeting, one of which came up after it.

threads.label: Frontiers and shipping after the three-power declaration
threads.text: Begun on 14 November: Zelensky said Washington floated Ukraine giving up Donbas for NATO membership as the three-power meeting was announced. On 19 November the Shenzhen declaration, by Observador's account, left out both wars and Putin invited Europeans to Moscow. On 20 November frontier states fortified: Estonia set 1 December to close its Russian crossings, Swedish jets flew over Poland and Kagoshima approved a Japanese base. On 21 November, marked plausible, it reached the sea: drones disabled the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, two tankers were hit leaving Hormuz, Iran shot down a US drone, and one of more than 110 Russian missiles was reported to hit Poland. Its case against says these attacks share timing, not a war or an attacker; the Hormuz events belong to the Iran thread's ground.
threads.direction: It has moved from Europe's security bargained in a format Europe does not lead, through allies seeking talks and then fortifying, to attacks on ships in the Gulf of Finland and off Hormuz after the declaration.

threads.label: Incomes set by rule falling behind prices
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. France had a fifth Saturday of protests against the cost of living and French police demanded a higher risk allowance; an Italian simulation put a 2028 pension more than 13,000 euros a year below one of twenty years earlier; a former Argentine judge warned of delays in retirees' claims, and a Canadian disability charity closed. The join is incomes fixed by law, decree or grant falling behind prices; its case against says the events share no cause. On 17 November a new thread on Europe's weekly protests took in the same French protest rounds and read them as met by top-ups; the Chronicle kept the two apart. No narrative has carried it since 14 November, so it is silent; on 19 November strikes outside Europe over pay owed began a thread of their own.

threads.label: Governments taking back roles in food supply
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked tentative that continues nothing. Nieuws.nl reports a fertiliser shortage caused by the Hormuz blockade threatening Dutch food security, Marib's farmers in Yemen have harvests and no open markets, Senegal calls rice a pillar of food sovereignty, New York is spending $70 million on five city-run grocery stores, Egypt's prime minister inspects a permanent state food fair, and Fortune reports nearby shops losing sales when Walmart leaves a town. The join is public authorities taking back choosing what is grown, securing inputs and selling food. Its case against says only the fertiliser story is new, Egypt's outlets date from the 1940s and New York's stores were a 2025 election promise. No narrative carried it on 17, 18 or 19 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to 5 and 12 December.

threads.label: Europe's protests over prices, met by top-ups
threads.text: Begun on 17 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts two weeks of protest over living costs and housing: 270,000 marched outside Paris on 6 November, Porto's housing camp put up tents on 8 November, Spain held its first general strike in 14 years on 11 November, and France counted 146,000 at a new round on 17 November. France brought forward a minimum wage rise and Italy's coalition argued over 300 euros for pensioners. Its case against says Spanish rents and French wages have different causes. No narrative has carried it since 17 November, so it is silent; on 20 November Gen Z marches across Europe and Bologna's general strike day came in the thread on young protesters.

threads.label: Defence decided by numbers of drones and interceptors
threads.text: Begun on 30 October with a narrative the Chronicle had not given a thread: cheap drones had made defence a matter of quantity again, so states were financing arms factories and widening conscription. After seventeen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 18 November, marked plausible, from the defending side: an Egyptian military expert told Al-Watan that closing the gap in US Patriot production will take years, the Jerusalem Post reported a rayon shortage threatening that production, Iran struck US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain and a UAE tanker, and a coalition struck the Houthis. Its case against says the Patriot shortfall has been discussed since 2023. No narrative carried it on 19, 20 or 21 November, so it is silent; on 21 November more than 110 Russian missiles struck Ukraine, in the thread on Europe's security, with no report on interceptor stocks.
threads.direction: It has moved from cheap drones driving arms production and conscription to interceptor stocks that factories cannot refill quickly.

threads.label: Others' trade deals while three powers meet
threads.text: Begun on 18 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing, as Trump, Xi and Putin were reported meeting in China. EU governments approved signing their trade agreement with Indonesia, Mark Carney bet on Asia-Pacific trade to reduce Canada's dependencies, Vietnam's leader called for a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, Xi asked Chile to deepen ties, Keiko Fujimori pitched Peru's Chancay port to Chinese investors and Egypt signed an industrial deal with India. The join is governments outside the meeting fixing their trade without waiting on it. Its case against says APEC leaders talk trade every November. On 19 November the meeting ended with a declaration that, by Observador's account, left out both wars, which weakens the picture of three powers bargaining over them. No narrative has carried trade since, so it is silent.

threads.label: Strikes outside Europe over pay already owed
threads.text: Begun on 19 November with a narrative marked tentative, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts strikes and protests outside Europe since 5 November in Nigeria, Egypt, Bangladesh, Canada, Chile, Mexico and South Korea: on 19 November Nigeria's lecturers demanded withheld salaries, Zamalek's players complained of late dues, Bangladeshi garment workers clashed with police and Niagara's paramedics neared a strike, while the World Bank said Bangladesh is short of revenue. The join is pay already earned or promised and not paid, often by a state short of money. Its case against says several headlines name no cause and the sample leans on three Nigerian papers. No narrative carried it on 20 or 21 November.

threads.label: States offering to site and underwrite data centres
threads.text: Begun on 20 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days, so the story is older than its first narrative. Trump threatened to tax or sanction US firms that build data centres abroad, Lagarde said EU funds should take first losses on chip plants and data centres, Google was reported to have cut a million TPU chips from its 2027 orders, CoreWeave fell below its listing price and the Nasdaq closed 5.37% lower. The join is governments offering to locate and carry the build as private investors sell. Its case against says CNBC reported Anthropic raising $93.5 billion the same day. No narrative carried it on 21 November, when a new thread read the wider fall, with gold and bitcoin, as the cost of money rather than the AI build alone.

threads.label: Young protesters met by police and courts
threads.text: Begun on 31 October with protests called for the same weekend in several European countries, met with bans in some cities and talks in others; on 1 November its edition read them as Europe's governments meeting young protesters mainly with police numbers. After seventeen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 20 November, marked plausible and built from the site's notebook: pupils in Schleswig-Holstein struck against conscription, DW reported Gen Z protests in hundreds of European cities, keeping a 31 October expectation of a shared protest date, a Lormont pupil went before the courts and France adopted its police weapons law, after a fortnight of arrests in Yogyakarta and Athens. Its case against says the protests share an age group, not a cause; no German ban has been reported. No narrative carried it on 21 November.
threads.direction: It has moved from police numbers set against young protesters to courts, arrests and suspensions, and in Germany to a plan for military service.

threads.label: Breaches of records people must give the state
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked firm, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for four days, so the story is older than its first narrative. Since 18 November attackers reached Transport for London's photocard records, the European Commission's servers through an AI-assisted attack, the FBI's National Crime Information Center database and the US Agriculture Department, beside leaks of over 10 million records at Japan's DHC and 15.18 million at ZOZOTOWN and thefts from four Taiwanese banks and Binance. The join is that public bodies make up about half the list, and people cannot withdraw records the state requires. Its case against says the breaches share dates, not an attacker, the FBI case rests on one AP source, and disclosure rules shape the balance. It continues nothing, though it sits near the systems thread's 17 and 18 November narratives.

threads.label: Gold, bitcoin and tech shares falling together
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. On 20 and 21 November the Nasdaq erased all its gains for the year, gold fell more than $2,000 an ounce from its peak, bitcoin dropped below $55,000 for the first time since September 2024 and foreign investors were reported pulling more than 3 trillion from Taiwan's market, as Trump attacked the Federal Reserve over rates and Italian buyers lost nearly 10% of their purchasing power to dearer mortgages. The join is the cost of borrowed money as a common cause, not the AI firms' troubles alone. It sits beside the data centre and AI financing threads, which read the same fall through chips and listings. Its case against says gold may be shedding a war premium after the Shenzhen declaration, and no margin calls are reported outside Taiwan.

threads.label: Power projects placed on water already promised
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked tentative, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for five days, so the story is older than its first narrative. On 21 November Amit Shah backed India's Siang dam and promised dialogue with protesters, after a Sharavathi submergence report was promised to the Supreme Court on 17 November and the court refused Tamil Nadu more Cauvery water on 20 November. Taipei's mayoral campaign has fought over solar panels on the Feicui reservoir, Finland's largest conservation project failed when a utility would not sell the Palokki plant, and Bogotá warned on 18 November of water and power rationing under El Niño. The join is new hydro and solar placed on water farms, towns and nature already count on. Its case against says half the evidence, Egypt's and Jordan's saving campaigns and Iraq's Habbaniyah flood, has nothing to do with power.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

withdrawn.held: On 30 October the Iran war's costs had turned towards easing, with Washington pressing for a lower oil price before the midterms.
withdrawn.undone: On 31 October Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64, Italy's inflation reached 5.4% and the price rise was argued over in pay rounds and tax relief in several countries. The easing reading did not last a day, and the earlier withdrawal of the outward-spread reading now looks premature.

withdrawn.held: The AI share sell-off was moving towards losses partly taken on by Taiwanese public money, through its state funds and central bank.
withdrawn.undone: On 1 November no state buying was reported, and the same thread was read as AI money landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron staff payouts and Chinese results led by AI computing. The public-money reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the thread's direction.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war thread had turned to which governments carry the fuel price and which take more of it as revenue, with US-Iran talks stuck.
withdrawn.undone: On 2 November no fuel-tax argument appeared, Brent fell 2% to $111, Trump said talks were going well and the thread was about whether a strike or talks follow the US vote. The who-pays reading rested on Turkey's single tax rise and is not carried as the direction; its expectation of a second government raising a fuel tax is still open.

withdrawn.held: The AI spending thread had turned to how narrowly the gains land, on a few chip and computing makers and their staff.
withdrawn.undone: Late on 2 November the thread was about the build depending on borrowing, with Oracle and Meta raising about $20 billion each and Anthropic losing more than its revenue, and on governments and voters setting terms for data centres; no payouts were reported. The concentration reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the direction; its expectations stay open.

withdrawn.held: Late on 2 November the Iran thread was tilting towards talks, with prices falling on leaders' words while incidents at sea continued.
withdrawn.undone: On 3 November the edition reported the strait still shut as the US struck Iran, with a bombing at Qeshm on polling day; Qatar's mediation went on, but the force was American, not only incidents at sea. The talks tilt held for one edition, and the thread returned to who pays and who gains from the closure.

withdrawn.held: Central banks abroad, Brazil's among them with the world's highest real interest rate, were holding rates high against the Iran war's oil price.
withdrawn.undone: On 5 November Mexico's central bank cut to 6.25% and Brazil's continued to cut while the Bank of England raised to 4%. Holding high describes some importers, not rate-setters in general, and the Mexican and Brazilian headlines do not name the war.

withdrawn.held: The contested-count thread had moved on from disputing results after a vote to acting before polling and contesting the bodies that run elections.
withdrawn.undone: On 6 November Liputan6 reported Trump saying the US election was rigged and Svenska Yle reported him demanding victory in Alaska's close Senate race. Disputing a result after the vote is back in these headlines, so the thread has not left it behind.

withdrawn.held: On 7 November the US-Iran war was going on, with the US reported striking Iran again and the Revolutionary Guards saying their missile range limits were lifted.
withdrawn.undone: On 8 November the edition reported the war as paused, with Trump calling a return to it very unlikely and pressure moved to Iraq's border crossings and a naval build-up. The fighting reported that day was between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, not between the US and Iran.

withdrawn.held: Since 3 November the Iran thread had been following who pays for the war's oil price, a question that passed on 7 November to the thread on fuel tax cuts.
withdrawn.undone: On 8 November the thread's narrative named no price, rate or tax, and followed pressure on Iran by land and sea and the Saudi-Houthi exchange. The price question is not carried as this thread's direction; it sits in the fuel tax thread.

withdrawn.held: On 8 November the question of the war's oil price had left the Iran thread and sat in the fuel tax thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 10 November the Iran thread's own narrative turned on price: Brent fell 5 per cent on Trump's words about talks, and exporters in Kenya and drivers in Vietnam were reported carrying the war's cost.

withdrawn.held: On 8 November the Iran thread was moving towards containing Iran by its land border with Iraq and a naval build-up.
withdrawn.undone: On 10 November the blockade was reported continuing, but the thread's narrative led with Trump's talk of momentum after meeting Qatar's prime minister and the oil price falling on it. No headline reported Iraq closing a crossing.

withdrawn.held: The reading of AI spending as gains concentrated on a few chip makers rested on one edition and was not carried as the thread's direction.
withdrawn.undone: On 10 November the thread returned on that reading: so much rests on Nvidia that Jensen Huang's admitted affair with an alleged spy moved its shares 8 to 9 per cent and US chip policy. The concentration reading now has two editions behind it.

withdrawn.held: The AI spending thread was moving from profit and borrowing to the market risk of resting so much on one chip firm, with share falls running on from 5 November.
withdrawn.undone: On the evening of 10 November its edition carried the Nvidia case on as espionage reached through people, beside a US officer arrested in Britain and leaked Norwegian phone numbers, while the market side, TSMC's stakes in AI labs and Nvidia's 12 per cent fall, came in a narrative not linked to it. The thread has turned out to be two.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise had reached the US ballot and cost Trump's party Congress.
withdrawn.undone: By 10 November no report on the midterm results or exit polls in these collections named fuel or energy prices as a reason, failing a 1 November expectation. The link rested on the 4 November narrative and on Trump tying the defeat to the war, not to the price.

withdrawn.held: The Nvidia case had passed from market risk to espionage reached through people, with the money side split off into a separate thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 12 November Huang's resignation was read as a risk of concentration on a few American suppliers, with AI shares falling from Bangkok to New York and Taiwan's suppliers counting the cost. The money side is back in the AI spending thread.

withdrawn.held: Governments were handing the war's fuel price back to drivers while the war went on, as Italy and Portugal ended or adjusted fuel tax discounts.
withdrawn.undone: On 12 November Pakistan cut petrol and diesel prices, Chile resubmitted a fuel price freeze to February and Greece paid €32 million toward island shipping costs. Governments were reported keeping pump prices in their own hands, not handing them back.

withdrawn.held: Huang's resignation and the Microsoft 365 outage were one thread about how much rests on a few American suppliers.
withdrawn.undone: On 13 November the edition gave Nvidia its own narrative, as a dispute between Treasury and Commerce over chips reaching China, and carried the outage on as public services running on single systems, beside the FAA's nationwide halt, which is a state system, not a supplier's.

withdrawn.held: Washington and Moscow were using Europe's place at the Ukraine talks as pressure, offering it on condition that Europe choose one negotiator.
withdrawn.undone: On 13 November the EU agreed to be represented by a team of five countries and EU institutions, joined by the coalition of the willing, and is joining the talks. The 11 November expectation of a single envoy failed, and the condition did not hold.

withdrawn.held: Since 8 November the Iran war had moved from fighting between the US and Iran to talks and a falling price.
withdrawn.undone: On 13 November Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain, and on 17 November the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian attacks on Bahrain. The US and Iran are reported striking each other again while talks are said to continue.

withdrawn.held: The AI spending thread carried both the money behind the AI build and the failures of shared systems, as one run from 29 October.
withdrawn.undone: On 18 November the edition carried the outages on alone, as patches for AI-found flaws, and gave Anthropic's record listing and the ECB's subprime comparison a narrative linked to neither. The Chronicle now keeps the money side in the thread on AI labs' financing.

withdrawn.held: At the meeting in China, Trump, Xi and Putin were bargaining over the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and over Europe's security, with Europe outside the room.
withdrawn.undone: On 19 November Observador reported that the Shenzhen 'declaration toward peace' left out both wars, and no report yet says NATO or nuclear weapons in Europe were discussed; Europeans met in Berlin and Putin invited them to Moscow. Lenta's report of Trump on the Crimean Bridge shows Ukraine came up, but not that it was bargained over.

withdrawn.held: By 19 November the thread on Europe's security was moving towards allies left out of the three-power meeting seeking their own talks with Moscow.
withdrawn.undone: On 20 November the same thread's narrative reported Estonia closing its Russian crossings from 1 December, Swedish jets over Poland, eleven armies drilling in Poland and a Japanese base approved, and no European call with Putin or trip to Moscow was reported. Talking and fortifying may run together, but the talks reading is not carried as the direction.

withdrawn.held: By 18 November the US and Iran were striking each other again while talks were said to continue.
withdrawn.undone: On 21 November Iran's Revolutionary Guard shot down a US drone over the strait in a report headed as Iran talks stalling, and two tankers were hit leaving Hormuz. The talks are no longer reported as going on alongside the strikes, and two expectations that oil would follow news of talks failed the same day.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on the editions since 26 October, with none stamped 28 October, 9 November or 15 and 16 November, drawn from whichever publishers the collection reads and capped in how many headlines each may supply. Of today's four narratives only one continues an earlier one, and that link carries the Hormuz tankers and the Iran drone into a thread about Europe's security although its own case against says the attacks share timing and not a war or an attacker; I keep the Iran thread silent by the rule on links, not because the Gulf has gone quiet. Two of today's threads were built from the site's notebook, so their several days of continuity are produced by the site, not by the editions. The gold and bitcoin thread sits beside two others that read the same 20 and 21 November fall through chips and listings, and these may be one market move split three ways by the rule on unlinked narratives. The breaches thread's public-private balance may reflect who must disclose, and the water thread is tentative with half its evidence not about power. I have now read the Shenzhen declaration as the hinge of the Europe thread for three days running, and that earlier framing pulls on how I placed today's ships.
line: On 21 November 2026, two days after the Shenzhen declaration, ships are hit in the Gulf of Finland and off Hormuz, and gold and bitcoin fall with the Nasdaq.
revision: Three threads were begun, on breaches of records held by public bodies, on gold, bitcoin and tech shares falling together, and on power projects placed on contested water. The thread on Europe's security was relabelled as it reached attacks on ships, the threads on shared systems, interceptors and trade deals fell silent, the reading of US-Iran talks continuing alongside strikes was withdrawn, and the standing was rewritten.
